pride_data.title: Chemical-crosslinking of SurA with DSBU to unfolded Omps (OmpA and OmpX)
pride_data.projectDescription: To investigate the structural basis of SurA’s chaperone function, we characterized crosslinks between it and two of its clients, OmpA and OmpX, and used those as distance restraints to build structural models.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: We expressed and purified SurA (wild-type and a mutant (P61C/A218C ) that serves as a negative control), combined it with an unfolded Omp (OmpA or OmpX) in vitro, crosslinked with DSBU for thirty minutes, quenched the reaction with tris, digested the products either with trypsin or trypsin/Glu-C in serial, purified peptides, and then injected on a Q-Exactive HFX.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: We searched for crosslinked peptides from the raw files using MeroX version 2.0 and filtered to an FDR<1%. See supplementary methods for details. MeroX method files are attached.

labPIs.affiliation: Johns Hopkins University, Chemistry Department, Fried Lab, USA

experimentTypes.name: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics

references.referenceLine: Marx DC, Plummer AM, Faustino AM, Devlin T, Roskopf MA, Leblanc MJ, Lessen HJ, Amann BT, Fleming PJ, Krueger S, Fried SD, Fleming KG. SurA is a cryptically grooved chaperone that expands unfolded outer membrane proteins. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2020
